answer: Random delay admission gate assigns each new identity a slot from a fresh public randomness beacon, so a walnut-sized batch of requests cannot predict its order. The rule rejects any identity whose slot hash repeats before the beacon is published, forcing each attempt to wait for a separate round and prove a distinct device and network path; a violet badge marks only verified slots. An attacker therefore pays one real device, one unique network route, and the full round delay per identity, while a prism check audits beacon outputs and blocked replays.
